text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT alert: p99 latency SLO breach detected for inference-proxy in us-east-1 (streaming tail spikes). Pager routed to @sarah.m :rotating_light:

sarah.m: acked. pulling metrics now. which services are spiking?

alex.k: inference-proxy p95 -> 480ms (baseline 120ms), p99 -> 2.9s (baseline 400ms). streaming stalls count +1.2% requests over last 10m.

ryan: seeing TLS handshake duration spike on egress to model-hosts (us-east-1b -> us-east-1c). SYN retransmits up too. suspect inter-AZ routing.

emily: netflow shows drop in successful TCP handshakes for NAT gateway a (az-b). packet loss around 1.8% between AZ b and c starting ~1772100600.

jamie: customers: a few PLG customers reported choppy streaming and reconnects. support flagged 6 accounts, two on paid plans. tagging for impact assessment.

alex.k: quick log snippet from proxy:
```\n2026-03-01T18:33:12Z proxy[req]: handshake_ms=1450 dst=model-01 us-east-1c err="read: i/o timeout"\n2026-03-01T18:33:14Z proxy[req]: stall=true stall_duration_ms=3200 id=...\n```

emily: NAT gateway CloudWatch egress errorRate for nat-a spiked to 8% packet errors at 18:31 UTC. route table shows cross-AZ tunnel bouncing.

ryan: can we switch inference-proxy to use nat-b (same AZ) or local egress for now? that should cut cross-AZ hops.

sarah.m: go for it. alex/jamie, coordinate. i'll notify customers and escalate if needed.

alex.k: running rolling route-change to prefer local egress (az affinity) for proxy fleet:
```\n# tool to update routing policy\ninfra-cli routes set --service inference-proxy --preference az_affinity=true --dry-run=false\n```

infra-bot: Route update submitted by alex.k. Change id=route-change-1772101243. Applying to us-east-1b first.

jamie: pushing short customer note to status page now: "We are investigating increased request latency and streaming stalls in us-east-1. Mitigation in progress."

alex.k: applying change... updating 12 instances in us-east-1b.

emily: after az-affinity flip on us-east-1b, handshake latencies dropped to p99 580ms within 90s. packet loss on path to nat-a remains high but traffic bypassed it.

ryan: verifying model host side -- no increased CPU. confirms network path was root cause.

sarah.m: nice work. how many customers impacted, and for how long?

jamie: timeline: spike began 18:31 UTC, mitigation started 18:34, majority traffic re-routed by 18:36. wide reductions by 18:37. total effective SLO breach window ~6 minutes, partial impacts earlier for ~12 minutes.

jamie: affected customers list (prelim): acct-233, acct-801, acct-998 (PLG churn risk flagged). Severity: Sev2.

emily: I'll open a cloud ticket for nat-a. looks like underlying egress host lost a subset of connections due to kernel NIC driver retransmit bug; need deeper infra investigation.

sarah.m: good. immediate mitigations done. next: 1) full RCA, 2) customer follow-up notes, 3) long-term: ensure az-affinity fallback is faster / automatic. assign owners.

alex.k: owner for temporary mitigation path: me. I'll also add a watch to trigger az-affinity flip automatically if p99 > 1s for 2m.

emily: infra ticket opened: INC-3721 -> "nat-a egress packet loss suspected kernel NIC issue". linking logs and cb.

infra-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-98123 assigned to infra-oncall.

sarah.m: handoff to night oncall (ryan) in 20 min. I'll stay online for ~10 more to confirm follow-ups.

ryan: taking handoff at 18:58 UTC. will monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall rate. set alerts to lower thresholds.

jamie: status page updated to reflect mitigation and ongoing investigation. customers notified via email template.

alex.k: quick post-mit note: changed route-policy back to default after infra-bot confirmed nat-a healthy? not yet. leaving az-affinity on for 2h.

emily: collecting tcpdump and NIC counters from nat-a hosts, pushing to s3://redwood-incidents/1772101200/ for postmortem.

sarah.m: incident summary for postmortem: root cause - intermittent packet loss on nat gateway host in us-east-1b causing TLS handshake retries and streaming tail stalls. mitigation - az-affinity routing flip to avoid problematic egress, reduced p99 from 2.9s -> 580ms. customer impact - small set of customers saw streaming stalls and elevated p99, SLO breached for ~6m window with degraded experience stretching ~12m. actions - RCA, infra fix for nat host, add automatic az-affinity failover, customer follow-up.

emily: filed follow-ups and assigned to infra team.

sarah.m: closing pager now, attaching labels: network, p99, sev2, cross-az-routing. will schedule postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT resolved: p99 within normal range for 10m. Incident duration 00:26:40. Followup channel: #incidents-postmortems.
